key_insight: A unified crystal plasticity-fracture model shows that creep cracking in metals transitions from trans-granular to mixed to inter-granular dominance as stress decreases, driven by competition between slip-induced intragranular cracking and grain-boundary cavitation.
engineering_relevance: This links microscale damage mechanisms to macroscopic creep rupture life and ductility, helping engineers predict when high-temperature components fail in ductile versus quasi-brittle modes.
method: Crystal plasticity coupled with grain-boundary cavitation
Crystallographic crack propagation within a unified fracture framework
evidence_signal: The abstract reports microscale computations across stress levels that reproduce systematic crack-mode transitions and associated changes in rupture ductility and creep life.
watch_item: The framework is computationally rich and likely needs careful calibration of grain-boundary and crack-propagation parameters for transfer to different alloys and loading conditions.
paper_title: Mechanistic transition between inter- and trans-granular creep cracking via a unified crystal plasticity-fracture framework
